title: Measuring One Instalment of Premium on a Protection Plan
content:
One instalment of premium on a Pass and Trip Protection plan is measured in one of three ways, according to
how the plan's premium is collected and what the covered holding's schedule still holds.

**Where the plan's premium is collected alongside the covered holding's instalments and instalments still fall
on its schedule**, one instalment is the premium still to be collected divided equally over the instalments
still to fall on that schedule, rounded to the cent.

**Where the plan's premium is collected in a single payment**, one instalment is the whole premium still to be
collected.

**In every other case**, one instalment is the premium still to be collected divided equally over the whole
months from the day cover began to the day cover is due to end, rounded to the cent.

**Points of judgement.** The first case asks two things together: that the plan is one whose premium rides on
the covered holding's instalments, and that instalments still fall on that holding's schedule. Where the plan
rides on those instalments but none still falls, the first case does not hold and the plan is not collected in
a single payment either, so the third governs and the whole months of cover are the divisor.

**Worked cases (hypothetical inputs).** A plan riding on the covered holding's instalments, 150.00 USD still
to be collected and 6 instalments still to fall on that schedule: one instalment is 25.00 USD. A plan
collected in a single payment with 150.00 USD still to be collected: one instalment is the whole 150.00 USD. A
plan riding on the covered holding's instalments with none still to fall, 150.00 USD still to be collected and
cover running 4 whole months from the day it began to the day it is due to end: one instalment is 37.50 USD.
